items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with right adjoint a of Rf_*, and L in D_QCoh(O_X), K in D_QCoh(O_Y), the lemma asserts that the map Rf_*RSheafHom_{O_X}(L, a(K)) -> RSheafHom_{O_Y}(Rf_*L, K) of equation labelled equation-sheafy-trace becomes an isomorphism after applying the functor DQ_Y of Derived Categories of Schemes, Section labelled perfect-section-better-coherator (statement lines 774-790). The statement makes sense because DQ_Y exists by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-better-coherator, and since DQ_Y is right adjoint to the inclusion D_QCoh(O_Y) -> D(O_Y) it suffices to show that for every M in D_QCoh(O_Y) the map induces a bijection on Hom_Y(M, -) (proof lines 792-804). The proof establishes this by a six term chain of equalities using, in order, the adjunction of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-adjoint, the internal Hom of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom, the construction of a, the base change formula of Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-cohomology-base-change, which the author marks as the important step, and the internal Hom again (proof lines 806-824). Recognising that the coherator is a right adjoint to the inclusion, so that it suffices to test on coherent objects, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
